errors.english: the Tathagatas [note: the Buddhas], who bring supreme light, performed the funeral rites
errors.why: The Sanskrit (tathāgatas) and the narrative make this the one Tathāgata, the Buddha, honouring his father Śuddhodana's body; plural 'the Buddhas' misidentifies the agent.

note: Faithful rendering of the verses on Śuddhodana's funeral and the monks' question; only the plural Tathāgatas misleads.

errors.english: If they cover it with boards, there is no offense.
errors.why: spang leb are turf/sod slabs, distinct from the wooden boards (shing leb) of the next clause.

note: Sound rendering of the Vinaya commentary on the building rule, with the Upāli quotation correctly handled.

errors.english: Because the delusion is similar.
errors.why: 'khrul pa here is the logical deviation (vyabhicāra) of the reason, which is the same in both cases, not 'delusion'.

fix.replace: Because the deviation (vyabhicāra) is the same.

errors.english: but the direction is not
errors.why: phyogs is the place/locus (cf. sa phyogs on the next side): fire, not the place, is the cause of smoke.

errors.english: Even if any particularity of wind and so forth is the cause, all particularities will not be endowed with all attachments and so forth; because at all times a definite result is seen, it is to be inferred.
errors.why: The whole argument from 'gal te rlung...' to 'yin pa'i phyir ro' is the anticipated objection, but the English presents its first part as the commentator's own statement.

note: Very literal and often opaque; key logical terms (vyabhicāra, locus) mistranslated and the scope of the objection blurred.

errors.english: Is born as a jewel among men, a blissful being.
errors.why: bde bar 'gro ba renders Sugata (Skt. prakaṭitasugataḥ), the Buddha epithet, not a generic 'blissful being'.

note: Colophon and opening verses of the next avadāna rendered well; the Sugata epithet is lost.

errors.english: when it perceives an appearance in what is called the (essential mind) tattva-buddhi
errors.why: The Tibetan refers to the cognition 'it is just that' (identifying judgement), not a technical 'tattva-buddhi / essential mind'.

errors.english: Because of the power of intense attachment
errors.why: lhag par zhen pa is adhyavasāya, conceptual determination, the key Pramāṇa term, not emotional attachment.

fix.find: Because of the power of intense attachment

errors.english: Not understanding the intention of others, externalists and so forth have spoken.
errors.why: The opponent ('the other'), not understanding the intention, raised the objection beginning 'the external ones'; phyi rol pa rnams is a lemma meaning external things (svalakṣaṇas), not non-Buddhist 'externalists'.

fix.find: Not understanding the intention of others, externalists and so forth have spoken.
fix.replace: Not understanding the intention, the other said "the external ones" and so forth.

errors.english: "Externalists from the generality" refers to the individual characteristics themselves.
errors.why: It glosses 'external' as 'external to the universal', i.e. the svalakṣaṇas; there are no 'externalists'.

fix.find: "Externalists from the generality" refers to the individual characteristics themselves.
fix.replace: "External" means external to the universal, that is, the individual characteristics.

errors.english: the commentators and others offer a reply
errors.why: The author replies by the root passage beginning 'the explainers (vyākhyātāraḥ)...'; the explainers are the subject of the quoted reply, not those who reply.

note: Core apoha/adhyavasāya vocabulary and the objection-reply structure are misread; needs a Pramāṇa specialist.

errors.english: downcast from pride, his lotus face became devoid of beauty
errors.why: With the previous side's ma bkur, this reads 'through that dishonour' (Skt. vimānena): the king is humiliated, not proud.

fix.find: downcast from pride, his lotus face became devoid of beauty
fix.replace: through that dishonour, the king's lotus face became devoid of beauty

note: Good verse translation of the king's distress and the sky-goddess's advice, apart from the opening phrase.

errors.english: Mimamsaka [note: original: "skyes mos", referring to the Mimamsa school of Indian philosophy]
errors.why: Mīmāṃsaka is dpyod pa ba in Tibetan; nothing supports reading skyes mos as the Mīmāṃsā school.

errors.english: is intended to be the producer of its own form. Therefore, to show that the object of observation here is nothing other than what is intended
errors.why: mngon par sems pa is abhimāna, the cognition's (false) conceiving/supposing of an object as the producer of its aspect, not 'intending'; the point is that its object is only something imagined.

note: Followable outline of the dream/waking pramāṇa argument, but the cognition's abhimāna and the opponent identification are off.

errors.english: That [note: absolute reality] is not of the same class as this [note: deluded appearance].
errors.why: The root says that is not fit to be reality (tattva), as the commentary's de nyid rigs pa ma yin confirms; 'same class' and the notes are invented.

fix.find: That [note: absolute reality] is not of the same class as this [note: deluded appearance].
fix.replace: That is not fit to be reality (tattva).

errors.english: regarding that very meaning which is characterized by equanimity—meaning the suchness that is free from defined characteristics and remains in equanimity—the Buddhas
errors.why: It is the Buddhas who are indifferent to (disregard) the meaning of reality (tattvārthopekṣa), not suchness that has equanimity.

fix.find: regarding that very meaning which is characterized by equanimity—meaning the suchness that is free from defined characteristics and remains in equanimity—the Buddhas
fix.replace: disregarding the meaning of reality—that is, treating with indifference the meaning of suchness, which is free from characteristics—the Buddhas

errors.english: [note: a steady, direct, and all-encompassing look]
errors.why: The elephant's look (gajanimīlikā) is feigned not-seeing, as the text itself explains; the note says the opposite.

fix.find: [note: a steady, direct, and all-encompassing look]
fix.replace: [note: gajanimīlikā, the elephant's feigned closing of the eyes: seeing but acting as if not seeing]

errors.english:
With a heart focused solely on the world,<-
->They engage in worldly conduct.
errors.why: The root says that solely through the world's understanding they engage in reasoning about external objects (bāhya), not 'worldly conduct' with a heart on the world.

errors.english: like a person desired [note: mental image or hallucination]
errors.why: mngon par 'dod pa'i skyes bu is the person accepted (in the opponent's example, the dreamt person), not a 'desired' person or hallucination.

note: The suchness / gajanimīlikā passage is turned around: equanimity given to suchness and the elephant's look glossed backwards.

errors.english: how does an understanding arise regarding the negation of the meaning of words as exclusion from things other than those non-exclusions?
errors.why: The question is how, from words that are not anyāpoha, a cognition arises that negates apoha as word-meaning; 'from' governs the words, not the exclusion.

note: Sound rendering of the apoha discussion on isolated words and siddhasādhana, with one garbled question.
Faithful rendering of the commentary on MMK 17.2-3 (cetanā and cetayitvā), with root verses correctly set off.
